mn146:3.2: The Comy. explains that Nandaka was reluctant because those bhikkhunīs had, in a past life, been his concubines when he was a king, and he feared that anyone recollecting past lives might accuse him of lingering attachment to them.
mn146:4.4: ‘Brahmin’ (brāhmaṇa) is used here as an honorific epithet for one who has banished evil, not a reference to caste.
mn146:6.7: Dukkha (‘painful’) has no single English equivalent covering all its senses: the sense bases, being impermanent and unreliable, are dukkha, yet it is in these very transient features of the world that people seek security, and so become further entangled in dukkha.
